name: Cross-Court Dink Rally
description: Stand at the kitchen line and sustain a cross-court dinking rally with a partner. Focus on soft hands, a continental grip, and keeping the ball below net height. Rally for 50 consecutive dinks before moving to backhand side.

name: Dink Toss Drill
description: Partner feeds soft balls into the kitchen while you practice controlled dinks back and forth. Focus on paddle angle and placement rather than speed. Builds consistency and ball control at the non-volley line.

name: Pickleball Dinking Technique – Lesson & Drill by Sarah Ansboury
description: In this week’s video I thoroughly cover Dinking Technique. I have combined the struggles I hear about most, with a lesson AND a few drills. Take a look and don’t forget to share it with someone else who could use a new dinking perspective.

name: Two Tap Drill
description: Stand at the kitchen line across from your partner and volley back and forth. When the ball comes to you, tap it up to yourself once before hitting it back. The goal is a consistent rally while controlling the pace of the ball — develops soft hands, reaction time, and volley consistency.

name: Wall Dink Drill
description: Position yourself three to four feet from a wall and softly tap the ball to simulate kitchen-line dinking. Emphasize minimal backswing, soft hands, a loose grip, and alternating forehand and backhand. Keep the ball below waist height on the wall.

name: Alternate Forehand & Backhand Wall Drill
description: Stand 10 feet from a wall and rally groundstrokes, alternating forehand and backhand on successive hits — direct backhands right and forehands left so the ball comes back to the opposite wing. Focus on shoulder turn, an abbreviated backswing, and adjusting your lead foot with each transition.

name: How To Play Skinny Singles – Lesson & Drill with Sarah Ansboury
description: When you play Skinny Singles as I recommend in the video, you end up using all the angles, much like you would during a game. Not only does that help you get better at playing your side of the court, it can make it easier to recognize what balls not to play.

name: Is There A Drill To Help Keep My Paddle Up?
description: This week in our ongoing Q&A Series I cover a few things to help you keep your paddle up and ready for that next shot.

name: Paddle Bounce Drill
description: Bounce the ball continuously on your paddle face, alternating between forehand and backhand sides. Variations: bounce while walking, alternate high and low bounces, or spin the paddle between bounces. Progress from 50 to 100 consecutive bounces. Builds hand-eye coordination and paddle feel.

name: Practice Your Erne – Mini-Drill with Sarah Ansboury
description: Most of the time players think the Erne is this incredibly difficult shot, it’s not as difficult as you might think. In this weeks video I want to show you (and your partner) a 2 person drill you can practice your Erne so you are better prepared when the opportunity shows itself in play.

name: Wall Rally Drill
description: Stand about eight feet from a solid wall and maintain a continuous rally. Progress through forehands only, then backhands only, then alternating. Count consecutive hits and try to set personal records — beginners target 20 consecutive hits, intermediates 50+. Keep an athletic stance, bent knees, and move your feet for balance.

name: Footwork Shadow Drill
description: Without a ball, practice match movement patterns from a ready position: 30 seconds of lateral shuffles, 10 split steps, 5 forward sprints to an imaginary kitchen line with backpedaling returns, and 30 seconds of crossover steps. Repeat the full sequence three times.

name: How To Practice Pickleball By Yourself: Mastering Solo Drills for Game Improvement
description: Today, we’re diving into a vital pickleball skill that can transform your gameplay: mastering movement and paddle control. These two components are essential in navigating the court effectively and making precise shots. I’ve got a fantastic single person drill that I love, and I’m eager to share why it’s so crucial for your game.

name: Shadow Movement Drill
description: Without a ball, move in sync with your doubles partner across the court — forward, back, and side to side as if tracking a rally. Teaches proper positioning, spacing, and doubles communication.

name: Return of Serve Deep Target
description: Server feeds consistent serves. Returner practices driving deep returns to the server's backhand corner. Goal: 8 of 10 returns land in the back third. Advance to kitchen after return.

name: Serve + Return Drill
description: One player practices consistent serves while the partner practices deep crosscourt returns. Builds shot reliability on the two most common shots in the game while reinforcing serve and return rules. Switch roles halfway through.

name: Serve and Stay In
description: Practice a consistent, deep serve targeting the back third of the service box. Partner returns; server focuses on a controlled third shot. Repeat 20 times each side. Consistency over power.

name: Serving From A Basket
description: Grab a basket of balls and practice serving until the basket is empty, focusing on consistency and placement. Collect the balls and repeat from the other side. Builds serve depth, placement, and the confidence to start every point well.

name: Target Serve Drill
description: Place a towel, cone, or bottle in the back third of the diagonal service box. Hit 20 serves aiming at the target, tracking how many land within a paddle-length of it. Use a relaxed underhand motion, contact below the waist, and follow through toward the target. Once you hit 15 of 20, move the target to develop placement variety.

name: Wall Serve Target Drill
description: Tape a one-square-foot box on a wall about 2 feet above net height. Stand 20 feet back and practice both drop serves and traditional serves into the target zone. Great solo serve practice when no court is available.

name: Directionality & Control at the Non-Volley Line – Mini-Lesson with Sarah Ansboury
description: Accuracy and shot placement are crucial winning points, your level of control and what I like to call directionality are how you improve your accuracy. In today’s video I cover an easy and important drill that will help you (and your practice partner) level up your control. Check it out… Pin it:.

name: Kitchen Line Volley Exchange
description: Both players at the kitchen line exchanging slow, controlled volleys. Goal is zero errors in 30 consecutive exchanges. Keeps paddle up, ready position after every shot.

name: Volley Reflex Drill
description: Stand about seven feet from a partner, both at the net, and volley continuously without letting the ball bounce. Start slowly and incrementally increase pace while maintaining control. Keep the paddle in front above waist height, use compact motions, and stay on the balls of your feet.

name: Attackable Balls & Disguising Shots Drill with Sarah Ansboury
description: Our focus in this week’s lesson/drill how to identify an attackable ball and what to do with it (think, what are my forehand directional options?), as well as how we can disguise our shot to keep the competition off balance or out of position. Today, we’re going to focus on improving our game.

name: Dink Patience Drill
description: Dink rally to 10 points using rally scoring, switching sides after each miss so you practice from the even side, odd side, and straight on. Forces consistency and removes the temptation to attack prematurely.

name: Dink Patterns: Straight and Cross
description: Partner drill: alternate between straight-ahead dinks and cross-court dinks in a structured pattern (2 straight, 2 cross). Helps develop shot placement awareness. Run for 5-minute sets.

name: Down the Line Dink Game
description: Partners face off at the kitchen line on half the court. One player feeds with a dink and the return must also be a dink — after that, anything goes: speed-ups, lobs, volleys, or attacks, all kept on the same half. Play best-of-three games to five points, then switch sides. Trains dink control, patience, and decision-making.

name: Walking Dinks
description: Wall drill for directional dink control: angle each dink slightly left or right off the wall so you have to step laterally with your shots. Travel about 10 feet in one direction, then reverse. Builds the ability to dink accurately while moving.

name: Creating A Poaching Opportunity – Pickleball Drill with Sarah Ansboury
description: Poaching is a process, that starts in the transition zone. Positioning with your partner is very important, your position and the rate you are moving is what dictates your ability to poach, and attack on those transitional balls. You and your partner both have a role and a job, if I’m hitting a 3rd shot.

name: Cross Court Drops
description: Partner stands at the kitchen line while you set up at the baseline cross-court from them. Hit drop shots toward your partner, who returns the ball deep. Do not move forward after your shot — stay behind the baseline. Target 10–20 successful consecutive drops, then switch sides.

name: Third Shot Drop from Baseline
description: From the baseline, hit a third shot drop into the non-volley zone. Partner catches or lets it bounce. Focus on a low, soft arc that lands in the kitchen. Complete 3 sets of 10 reps each side.

name: Three and Go — Baseline
description: Apply the reset concept from the baseline: hit drop shots under pressure from a partner at the net, requiring three quality drops minimum before you're allowed to advance. Emphasizes margin over perfection — a good-enough drop you can follow in beats a perfect one you can't repeat.

name: Transition Zone Drop and Advance
description: Start at mid-court (transition zone). Hit a drop shot into the kitchen then advance to the kitchen line. Partner resets the ball from the kitchen. Repeat, practicing the split-step timing as you advance.

name: Putting Pressure On Your Pickleball Opponents – Lesson & Drill By Sarah Ansboury
description: That’s a question I get often, and this week I not only want to answer your question but I want to show you a drill I use with my students that helps make the concept of “applying pressure” into reality, improving muscle memory so it becomes a natural part of your game. Also, this is.

name: Wall Lobs
description: Position close to a wall and generate substantial height on your shots to simulate lobs from the kitchen area. Focus on a smooth lifting motion and consistent height control so the lob clears an opponent's reach but stays in the court.

name: Backhand Reset Under Pressure
description: Partner speeds up balls at your backhand from the kitchen. Your job is to absorb the pace and drop the ball softly into the kitchen — a reset. Focus on giving with the paddle on contact. 3 sets of 15.

name: Short Hop Shots
description: Stand five feet from a wall, parallel to it, and let the ball bounce near your feet before hitting it — a half-volley. Use minimal backswing and angle shots softly upward. Trains handling of awkward low bounces at your feet, a key transition-zone skill.

name: Speed Control Wall Drill
description: Against a wall, hit one or two firm volleys and then immediately attempt a gentle dink. Develops the ability to convert a fast incoming ball into a controlled soft shot — the core skill behind blocks and resets.

name: Speed-Up and Reset Drill
description: One player speeds up a ball at the net; the partner works on resetting it into a soft dink. Trains reflexes, pressure response, and reset execution. Swap roles every few minutes.

name: Three and Go — Transition
description: Stand in the transition zone while your partner pressures you with balls below the waist. You must hit a minimum of three quality resets before advancing to the net. Builds the patience and soft hands needed to work through mid-court under fire.

name: Mastering Weight Transfer for Powerful Volleys
description: One of the most overlooked aspects of a strong volley is weight transfer. If you’re not engaging your lower body properly, you’re missing out on power, control, and consistency. That’s why I love this drill—it helps you learn how to shift your weight efficiently through the ball, improving both your shot execution and recovery.

name: Moving Volley Drills
description: Practice both forehand and backhand volleys while moving laterally across the court. Partner feeds balls that force you to shuffle between shots. Builds the ability to volley cleanly while repositioning instead of only from a static stance.

name: Volley Hands Control
description: Partner hits volleys at you at 60–75% power, moving the ball around without attempting winners. Focus on compact strokes and keeping the paddle in front of your shoulders. Builds hand speed and control without competitive pressure.

name: Wall Volley Speed Drill
description: Stand five to six feet from a wall and volley as rapidly as possible without losing control — no bounces allowed. Keep the paddle up and in front, use wrist and forearm rather than shoulder, and stay light on your feet. Start with 30-second intervals, building to one minute.

name: Fake-Out Attack
description: Set up a high ball as if attacking with an aggressive volley, then reduce paddle speed at the last moment to softly dink instead. Trains shot disguise and tactical deception — opponents who brace for the speed-up get caught leaning.

name: Fifth Shot Aggression
description: After your opponent returns your third shot, stay aggressive on the fifth shot instead of automatically resetting. Play out serve, return, third, and fifth in sequence, choosing the attacking option whenever the ball allows. Trains maintaining attack momentum through the point.

name: Initiator Attack Game
description: One player (the initiator) is allowed to attack off the bounce or out of the air at any time; the opponent may only counter. Develops offensive aggression and defensive patience simultaneously. Switch roles after each game.

name: Speed-Up Attack and Counter
description: Player A speeds up a ball at Player B's body. Player B counters back at Player A's feet. Rally continues until someone misses or resets. Develops quick reflexes and body-ball recognition. 5-minute continuous play.

name: Speed-Up Game: Two Dinks Then Live
description: Players must execute exactly two dinks before anyone may attack, then the point is live. Forces patience, teaches you to identify which balls are actually worth attacking, and trains point construction from the kitchen line.

name: Transition Attack Drill
description: Partner feeds short balls; you attempt aggressive drives from the transition area. Goal is winning one of every three attempts. Trains recognizing and converting offensive opportunities on the move.

name: Competitive Dinking with Speed-Up Option
description: Cross-court dinking rally where either player can speed up at any time. The other player must counter or reset. Play to 11 points. Builds patience and the ability to recognize and create opportunities.

name: Moving Dink Positioning
description: Practice dinking when the ball doesn't come to your optimal sweet spot — partner deliberately varies placement so you must move your feet into proper position before every dink rather than reaching. Builds positioning discipline on the move.

name: Rapid Recovery Dinking
description: Focus on the three parts of every shot: receiving, sending, and recovery. Dink with a partner while practicing closing gaps in the middle and recovering back to center position after each shot so the whole court stays covered.

name: Advanced Third Shot Drop Sequences
description: Baseline player hits third shot drops until one lands in the kitchen and is unattackable, then advances. Kitchen player applies pressure — speeds up anything above the net. Measures quality of drop under pressure. Competitive scoring.

name: Drive and Drop
description: Receive a deep ball, drive it, stabilize, then hit a fifth-shot drop before advancing. Mirrors real match sequencing where the third-shot drive sets up the fifth-shot drop. Trains baseline offense followed by controlled transition.

name: Third-Shot Drops with Spin
description: Practice third shot drops while adding topspin and backspin variations. Topspin drops dip faster and are harder to attack; backspin drops die lower after the bounce. Work both forehand and backhand from varying court depths.

name: Modified 7-11: Baseline to Kitchen
description: One player starts at the baseline, the other at the kitchen. The baseline player can only win points while at the baseline, forcing them to earn their way forward on every point instead of camping at the kitchen line. Trains the full transition game under match pressure.

name: Poaching Drill
description: Set up crosscourt rallies in doubles formation and practice timing your movement across the middle to intercept (poach) a ball. Trains anticipation, timing, and partner coordination — communicate before and after every poach attempt.

name: Defensive Lob Drill
description: Opponents lob over one player; the partner covers, returning either overheads or defensive resets. Trains lob defense, overhead decision-making, and the switch-and-cover communication that lobs force in doubles.

name: Lob Retrieval Drill
description: Players dink normally, but either player can throw up an unexpected lob at any time. The lobbed player must let it bounce, track it down, and play the point out. Chaotic in the best way — builds lob defense, court awareness, and mental readiness.

name: Overhead Defense Drill
description: Partner feeds deeper balls that you lob back over the net. After each lob, you play defense while the feeder attempts overheads. Builds offensive lobbing and defensive scrambling in a single exercise.

name: Serve Counter Drill
description: One player serves aggressively while the other volleys from the net, then the point plays out. Works serve placement, counter volleys, court shading, and middle-court vulnerability — the server learns which targets earn weak replies.

name: Erne Setup and Execution
description: Practice the Erne: dink cross-court to pull opponent wide, then jump around the post or step through the kitchen corner to volley from outside the NVZ. Shadow practice 10 times then live reps with a feeding partner.

name: ATP and Roll Volley Combination
description: Advanced tournament drill: partner feeds wide balls to practice the Around-The-Post (ATP) shot followed immediately by a roll volley to the open court. Execute 20 reps each side with correct footwork and follow-through.

name: Backhand Flick vs. Roll
description: Isolate the two backhand speed-up weapons: the flick (wrist-driven, off the bounce) and the roll (topspin, out of the air). Alternate reps of each off partner feeds at the kitchen line, learning which situations call for which. Adds disguise and variety to your attacking options.

name: Fireball
description: One player feeds hard shots from the baseline to a partner at the net line and attempts to advance behind them; the net player works to keep the feeder back with deep, controlled volleys. Simulates low drives against a net defender. Play to 11 points, then switch roles.

name: Terminator
description: Net player feeds a high, attackable ball to the baseline player, who attacks with an aggressive drive (simulating a third-shot drive). The net player counters at the baseline player's feet and the rally continues on half-court. Run down-the-line and crosscourt variations. Play to 11 points, then switch roles.

name: Volley, Surprise Lob & Overhead
description: Wall sequence drill: execute multiple high-speed volleys, follow with a surprise lob, then finish with an overhead smash. Trains the full offensive sequence of pressuring with pace, changing trajectory, and putting the ball away.

name: Spin Dink and Volley Series
description: Wall series combining spin dinks with volleys on both wings: backspin dinks (slight downward motion — ball comes back lower), topspin dinks (brush up — ball comes back higher), and sidespin dinks (outside-to-inside motion — adjust your target for lateral movement), each followed by a volley. Trains advanced spin control and rapid soft-to-firm transitions.

name: Full-Court Scenario Game Simulation
description: Professional-level competitive rally simulation: points start with a serve and play out at full pace. Emphasis on pattern play — third shot, advance, reset if needed, find and attack the first pop-up. Analyze patterns after each point. Best of 21.

name: Overhead Angle Placement
description: Partner feeds lobs; practice hitting overheads to sharp angles rather than straight ahead — short angle crosscourt, at the feet of the deep player, and to the open sideline. Trains finishing points with placement instead of raw power.

name: Survivor
description: Baseline player feeds a lob to the net player, who smashes and attempts to end the point; the baseline player's job is to survive and extend the rally. Conducted across half-court in all directions. Play to 11 points, then alternate roles. Elite defense and overhead training in one drill.

name: Serve plus Tournament Pattern Play
description: Professional serve targeting: practice power serves to T, body, and wide positions, each followed by a planned third shot pattern (drop vs. drive decision based on return depth). Full match-simulation pressure with scoring.

name: High-Level Firefight Training
description: Both players at kitchen line engaging in rapid-fire speed-up exchanges. No resets allowed — must counter or win the point. Trains competitive fast-hands reflexes at professional pace. 10-point games with full tracking.

name: High-Speed Wall Volleys
description: Stand near a wall and hit forehand volleys, then backhand volleys, as rapidly as possible while maintaining accuracy, finishing with an alternating pattern. Elite hand-speed conditioning for firefights — target 50 consecutive hits without error.
